title: The Farewell Party
description: Arjun faces pressure from friends at a terrace party. Practise a calm refusal and exit plan.

scenes.narration: Terrace farewell party. Music is playing in the background.
scenes.speaker: Rohan
scenes.quote: Come on, everyone is trying it. Don't be boring!

choices.subtitle: Stay firm and respectful
choices.feedback: A calm, firm no is hard to argue with. You don't owe anyone an explanation.

choices.subtitle: Find something else to do
choices.feedback: Changing the plan gives everyone an easy way out and keeps things friendly.

choices.subtitle: Walk away if needed
choices.feedback: Stepping away is always an option. You can come back later or head home.

choices.subtitle: Do what the group is doing
choices.feedback: Many people feel this pull. Practising gives you a plan for next time. Let's look at what you could do.

scenes.narration: The moment passes, but Arjun feels uneasy.
scenes.speaker: Arjun
scenes.quote: I wish I had a plan. What can I do next time?

choices.subtitle: For example: "Not for me, thanks."
choices.feedback: A ready-made line makes it much easier to speak up in the moment.

choices.subtitle: Share how I feel
choices.feedback: Talking it through with someone you trust is a strong step.

choices.subtitle: I'll think about it later
choices.feedback: That's okay. You can replay this scenario any time.

scenes.narration: Rohan pushes a little harder.
scenes.speaker: Rohan
scenes.quote: Bro, one time won't hurt.

choices.text: I'm not judging you. It's just not for me.
choices.subtitle: Calm and respectful
choices.feedback: You respected him and still held your ground. That's a strong response.

choices.text: Let's go listen to the music instead.
choices.subtitle: Change the subject
choices.feedback: Redirecting keeps the mood light and moves attention elsewhere.

choices.text: That's stupid. Don't do it either.
choices.subtitle: Argue back
choices.feedback: Being firm is great, but arguing can start a fight. Try keeping it about you: "not for me".

scenes.narration: Rohan shrugs. Meera joins the group.
scenes.speaker: Meera
scenes.quote: We were about to get some food downstairs. Coming?

choices.subtitle: Go along with the new plan
choices.feedback: A new plan gives everyone something better to do.

choices.subtitle: Bring more friends
choices.feedback: Bringing others along makes the new plan easy to follow.

scenes.narration: Arjun steps away from the crowd and takes out his phone.
scenes.speaker: Arjun
scenes.quote: I'll text Meera. She'll understand.

choices.subtitle: Ask a trusted friend to help
choices.feedback: Asking a trusted person for help gives you an easy, natural reason to leave.

choices.subtitle: Leave without a fuss
choices.feedback: Leaving quietly is a valid choice. You don't need to explain yourself.

scenes.narration: Later that night, Arjun thinks about how it went.
scenes.speaker: Arjun
scenes.quote: Saying no gets easier with practice.
scenes.takeaway: Saying no is a skill, and skills improve with practice.

title: Group Chat Dare
description: A late-night dare lands in your batch group. Practise setting a digital boundary.

scenes.narration: A late-night ping in your batch group chat.
scenes.speaker: Class group
scenes.quote: Who's brave enough to try it tomorrow at the back bench? Reply with a fire emoji!

choices.subtitle: Short, clear and friendly
choices.feedback: A short, friendly reply often gives quieter classmates permission to say no too.

choices.text: Mute the chat for the night
choices.subtitle: Step away from the pressure
choices.feedback: Digital boundaries count. Not reacting takes away the audience.

choices.text: Send a laughing emoji to blend in
choices.subtitle: Avoid standing out
choices.feedback: Blending in is a common reflex. Even a reaction can keep a dare going. Let's look at other options.

scenes.narration: Next morning, a classmate messages you privately.
scenes.speaker: Kavya
scenes.quote: I didn't want to do it either. What should I say?

choices.subtitle: "Just say it's not your thing."
choices.feedback: Helping a friend find their words is a strong, supportive move.

choices.subtitle: Plan lunch at the canteen
choices.feedback: A better plan makes it easy for both of you to skip the dare.

choices.text: Tell her to talk to someone she trusts
choices.subtitle: A friend, sibling or mentor
choices.feedback: Pointing someone toward trusted support is always a good option.

scenes.narration: The group chat moves on to exam notes.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: That was easier than I expected.
scenes.takeaway: You can set boundaries online just as clearly as in person.

title: Hostel Night
description: A roommate offers a shortcut for an all-nighter. Practise choosing your own routine.

scenes.narration: 1:30 AM in the hostel corridor. Exams start tomorrow.
scenes.speaker: Vikrant
scenes.quote: Seniors say this helps you study all night. Want some?

choices.text: No thanks, I'll take a short nap
choices.subtitle: Stick to your own routine
choices.feedback: Saying no and naming your own plan makes the answer feel natural.

choices.text: Head to the quiet study hall
choices.subtitle: Change your surroundings
choices.feedback: Moving to a different space is a simple way to step out of pressure.

choices.text: Maybe just a little to test it
choices.subtitle: Go along with it
choices.feedback: Never take something when you don't know what it is. Let's practise another way.

scenes.narration: Vikrant follows you out, looking stressed.
scenes.speaker: Vikrant
scenes.quote: Honestly, I'm panicking about this paper.

choices.subtitle: Study side by side
choices.feedback: Turning pressure into a shared plan helps both of you.

choices.text: Suggest he call someone he trusts
choices.subtitle: Family or a close friend
choices.feedback: Talking to someone trusted can ease stress a lot.

choices.text: Say goodnight and go to sleep
choices.subtitle: Look after yourself first
choices.feedback: Rest is a valid choice. Looking after yourself matters.

scenes.narration: Morning. You walk into the exam hall rested.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: My own routine works for me.
scenes.takeaway: Your own routine is a choice you can stand by.

title: After the Match
description: Your team wins the trophy and the celebration gets pushy. Practise staying true to your game.

scenes.narration: Your team just won the inter-college trophy.
scenes.speaker: Captain
scenes.quote: Champs celebrate hard! Join in or you're not really one of us.

choices.text: I'm good, I'll celebrate my way
choices.subtitle: Firm and friendly
choices.feedback: You celebrated the win and kept your choice. Both can be true.

choices.subtitle: Suggest a team dinner
choices.feedback: A team dinner keeps the celebration going without the pressure.

choices.text: My family is waiting at the gate
choices.subtitle: Head out gracefully
choices.feedback: A graceful exit lets you leave on a high note.

scenes.narration: A teammate catches up with you later.
scenes.speaker: Teammate
scenes.quote: Was the captain annoyed? I didn't want to join either.

choices.text: "It's fine. We can say no and still be a team."
choices.subtitle: Reassure them
choices.feedback: Showing that a no doesn't break friendships is powerful.

choices.subtitle: Focus on the next match
choices.feedback: Shared goals keep a team close.

scenes.narration: Monday practice. The team is back on the field.
scenes.speaker: Coach
scenes.quote: Good focus today, everyone.
scenes.takeaway: You can celebrate a win and still make your own choices.

title: Cousin's Wedding
description: Older cousins push you at a family function. Practise a respectful exit.

scenes.narration: Behind the wedding tent, older cousins call you over.
scenes.speaker: Cousin
scenes.quote: You're in college now. Try it, nobody inside will know!

choices.subtitle: Short and respectful
choices.feedback: A short, respectful no works with family too.

choices.text: Uncle asked me to help with the music
choices.subtitle: Use a family duty
choices.feedback: A real task is a natural reason to step away.

choices.subtitle: Bring them back to the party
choices.feedback: Redirecting back to the celebration keeps the mood happy.

scenes.narration: Your younger cousin saw what happened.
scenes.speaker: Younger cousin
scenes.quote: What would you do if they ask me next year?

choices.subtitle: "Not for me, thanks."
choices.feedback: You just passed on a skill. That's leadership.

choices.subtitle: Be a trusted person
choices.feedback: Being someone's trusted person is a big deal.

scenes.narration: Back on the dance floor with the family.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: That felt good.
scenes.takeaway: A respectful no protects both you and your relationships.

title: The Cool Senior
description: A senior you admire sets a condition for joining their team. Practise a professional boundary.

scenes.narration: A respected senior invites you to their project team.
scenes.speaker: Senior
scenes.quote: We all do this before brainstorming. Join us if you want to be in the core team.

choices.text: I'd love to join, but that's not for me
choices.subtitle: Keep it about your skills
choices.feedback: You showed interest in the work and kept your boundary. That's professional.

choices.text: Can we brainstorm in the lab?
choices.subtitle: Suggest another way
choices.feedback: Offering a different setting keeps the door open.

choices.text: I have a deadline, see you later
choices.subtitle: Step away for now
choices.feedback: Stepping away avoids being cornered. You can follow up later.

scenes.narration: The next day, the senior messages you.
scenes.speaker: Senior
scenes.quote: No pressure. Can you share your design ideas?

choices.subtitle: Let your work speak
choices.feedback: Good teams value skills, not going along.

choices.text: Ask a mentor for advice first
choices.subtitle: Get a second opinion
choices.feedback: Checking with someone you trust is a smart move.

scenes.narration: Your design makes it into the final project.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: My work speaks for itself.
scenes.takeaway: Real respect comes from your skills, not from going along.

title: Stressed Before Exams
description: Someone offers a quick fix for exam nerves. Practise healthier ways to cope.

scenes.narration: Your hands are shaking before the hardest paper.
scenes.speaker: Senior
scenes.quote: You look stressed. Take this, it calms you down instantly.

choices.text: No thanks, I'll take a few slow breaths
choices.subtitle: Use your own way to calm down
choices.feedback: Slow breathing and water are simple ways many people use to settle nerves.

choices.text: Call my sister for a minute
choices.subtitle: Reach out to someone you trust
choices.feedback: Hearing a familiar voice can be very steadying.

choices.subtitle: Accept the quick fix
choices.feedback: Exam nerves are very common. Never take something unknown. Let's practise other ways to cope.

scenes.narration: Ten minutes until the exam starts.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: What helps me focus right now?

choices.subtitle: Trust your preparation
choices.feedback: Focusing on what you know builds calm confidence.

choices.subtitle: Reset your body
choices.feedback: A short walk is a simple reset.

scenes.narration: You finish the paper and step out into the sun.
scenes.speaker: You
scenes.quote: I handled that my way.
scenes.takeaway: Healthy ways to cope with stress get stronger every time you use them.
